name: Mercat Cross
description: A market cross first recorded in a charter of 1365, historically the spot from which Edinburgh's royal proclamations were read and, for centuries, the symbolic heart of the burgh's civic and trading life. name: Edinburgh City Chambers
description: Built from 1753 as the Royal Exchange, a grand quadrangle designed by John Adam (with amendments by John Fergus) meant to lure Edinburgh's merchants off the street and into proper trading rooms, funded by public subscription and opened by Lord Provost George Drummond in 1760. It never really worked: merchants kept right on doing business at the Mercat Cross outside, so the Town Council gradually took the building over instead, buying its north range as council offices in 1811 and the rest by 1893. It has served as Edinburgh's seat of local government - Town Council, Corporation, District Council and now City of Edinburgh Council - ever since.

Category A listed since 1970, the Chambers' quadrangle has also stood in for other cities on screen, doubling as Stirling in Braveheart (1995) and appearing in the TV series Belgravia (2019).

name: Parliament House
description: Built between 1632 and 1640 to a design by James Murray, the Crown's Master of Works, this was the world's first purpose-built parliament building, raised so Scotland's Parliament, Court of Session and other courts could finally leave their cramped, shared quarters inside St Giles' and the old Tolbooth. description: The High Kirk of Edinburgh has stood on this site since at least 1124, though the present Gothic building mostly dates from the 14th and 15th centuries, crowned by a distinctive open crown steeple built around 1460-1467 - one of only two such medieval crown spires surviving in Scotland.
